name: Clear aligners
lead: Clear aligners are removable, transparent plastic orthodontic appliances that move teeth in small steps through a series of trays, each shaped slightly differently from the last. A digital scan or impression of the teeth is used to plan the movements in software, and a new aligner is typically worn for one to two weeks and for about 22 hours a day. [1] Align Technology's Invisalign, which began US sales in 1999, is the best-known system; many other brands, including dentist-supervised and direct-to-consumer services, now exist. [1][2][3]

Aligners are used to straighten crowded or spaced teeth and to correct some bite problems, with the appeal that they are far less visible than metal braces and can be removed for eating and cleaning. [1][4] Wikipedia describes them as indicated mainly for mild to moderate crowding or spacing of roughly 1 to 6 mm in cases without jaw discrepancies, and as likely less effective than conventional braces for some movements such as rotations and tooth-position changes. [1]

The scientific literature includes several systematic reviews, and their conclusions are qualified. A 2015 systematic review identified methodological shortcomings in the available studies, and later reviews and meta-analyses compare aligners with fixed appliances across malocclusion types and in extraction cases. [5][6][7] A 2022 review stated that tooth-movement accuracy with aligners relative to prediction was around 50 percent, whereas fixed appliances fared better. [8] Orthodontic organisations including the American Association of Orthodontists have raised concerns about direct-to-consumer services that do not involve in-person supervision by a dentist. [1]

paras: Treatment begins with diagnostic x-rays and photographs and capture of the bite and teeth by impressions or an intraoral scanner, and the dentist or orthodontist writes a treatment plan. A technician or software moves the teeth virtually through intermediate stages, and a digital preview, in Align's system called ClinCheck, is shown to the clinician and patient for approval before aligners are made. [1] Bonded composite attachments are often added to teeth to help the plastic grip and produce particular movements, and a 2022 systematic review examined the effect of composite attachments on aligner therapy. [1][9]

A 2023 review lists the advantages of clear aligner therapy as near invisibility, comfort and removability for eating and brushing, and notes that Invisalign was initially available only to orthodontists but was later extended to general dentists. [10] A 2017 review noted at least 27 different clear aligner products on offer. [2] The material and design of aligners have been reviewed in the bioengineering literature. [11] Biomechanical studies have measured the forces and moments generated by aligners for incisor torque, premolar derotation and molar distalization. [12]

A 2017 review traces removable appliances analogous to clear aligners to the Tooth Positioner introduced in 1944, with modern clear aligner therapy becoming widespread after Invisalign's introduction in 1998. [2] Wikipedia says Align Technology was founded in 1997 by Zia Chishti, who conceived the idea as an adult orthodontic patient wearing a retainer; sales began in the US in 1999, orthodontists were initially resistant, and by 2014 some 80,000 dentists had been trained to use the system. Align reports having treated more than 12.2 million patients. [1]

Chishti left Align in 2002 and developed a competing product, Orthoclear, in 2005, leading to patent and other legal disputes that were settled in 2006 with Align paying Orthoclear $20 million and Orthoclear ceasing operations. Dentist Willis Pumphrey then founded ClearCorrect in 2006 to complete his patients' treatment; Straumann acquired it in 2017. SmileDirectClub, launched in 2014, offered direct-to-consumer aligners from home at about half the competitors' price, and drew criticism from orthodontic groups over the absence of a physical dentist. In 2009 Align began requiring Invisalign providers to treat at least ten cases a year and complete training, and about 20,000 doctors had their certification suspended in 2010. [1]

A 2015 systematic review found 11 relevant studies and highlighted methodological shortcomings, and Wikipedia notes that a 2014 review concluded the published evidence was insufficient to determine effectiveness. [1][5] An earlier prospective study of 37 patients measured predicted versus achieved movement of 401 anterior teeth, and a 2020 follow-up study of 38 patients using intraoral scans examined whether accuracy had improved. [13][14] A 2014 study of 30 patients examined incisor torque, premolar derotation and molar distalization and the influence of attachments and staging. [15]

Systematic reviews of effectiveness include an Invisalign-focused review in 2018, a 2020 review of clear aligner therapy, and a 2017 meta-analysis of efficiency, effectiveness and stability. [16][17][18] A 2023 systematic review compared aligners with fixed appliances in complicated and severe malocclusions, a 2025 systematic review compared them for anterior teeth in adults, and a 2025 meta-analysis compared effectiveness across malocclusion types. [19][20][7] A 2019 comparative study and a 2005 outcome assessment using the American Board of Orthodontics grading system compared aligner and traditional treatment results. [21][22] A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis examined aligners in extraction-based treatment. [6]

A 2022 review on biomechanics argued that accuracy of tooth movement versus prediction was around 50 percent, and described vigorous advertising of aligners to patients and clinicians on social media. [8] Wikipedia reports that aligners are generally considered useful for moderate front-tooth crowding and that relapse of anterior teeth has been found more frequently than with conventional braces. [1]

Controlled trials include a randomized trial of 40 adults with anterior open bite comparing clear aligners with fixed appliances plus miniscrews for molar intrusion, measuring root resorption, intrusion and bite force at six months. [23] A randomized trial compared Invisalign First phase I treatment with tooth-borne rapid maxillary expansion in mixed-dentition patients for palatal volume and surface area. [24] A randomized trial compared periodontal health and quality of life with aligners versus fixed appliances after orthognathic surgery, and another randomized trial compared finished case quality between Invisalign and fixed appliances. [25][26] A 2006 clinical trial examined finishing with Invisalign, and a randomized trial examined clear aligners and sleep bruxism. [27][28] An editorial discussed the transparency of Invisalign. [29]

The reviews cited above point to variable predictability for certain tooth movements. Reported risks in the literature include relapse after treatment, root resorption, which one trial measured in aligner and fixed-appliance molar intrusion, and gum and periodontal effects, which another trial assessed after orthognathic surgery. [1][23][25] Outcomes depend on wear time, and aligners are removable. [1][10] Wikipedia notes that aligners are not recommended for children in conventional use, and the American Association of Orthodontists issued a consumer alert about direct-to-consumer services lacking in-person supervision. [1]

Wikipedia reports that prices in Australia, Canada, the United States and the United Kingdom are fairly similar across providers at about $2,000 or 1,500 pounds, and that aligners are typically less costly than all-metal braces; the exact cost depends on the treatment plan, age, location and clinician. [1]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org, clear aligners are discussed as an alternative to braces, with recurring questions about gum recession, palate expansion, overbite and jaw position, and about whether aligners address skeletal problems.[30][31][32][33]

claims.claim: Braces cause gum recession, so Invisalign is the safer choice for facial structure.
claims.believers: Users ask whether braces would cause recession and whether Invisalign could, and one reply advises Invisalign for the poster's mild case.[30][31][33]
claims.experts: Reported risks in the aligner literature include relapse, root resorption and gum and periodontal effects, and one randomized trial compared periodontal health with aligners versus fixed appliances after orthognathic surgery.[1][23][25] The sources reviewed do not report a head-to-head recession comparison for general patients.

claims.claim: Invisalign can expand the palate slightly while straightening teeth.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org user asks whether Invisalign would "expand my palate slightly" to correct their teeth.[30]
claims.experts: A randomized trial compared Invisalign First phase I treatment with tooth-borne rapid maxillary expansion in mixed-dentition children for palatal volume and surface area.[24] The sources reviewed do not report skeletal palate expansion in adults from aligners.

claims.claim: Aligners alone cannot fix a larger overbite, which needs a Herbst or Forsus appliance.
claims.believers: A reply on looksmax.org says aligners "can only do so much" for a severe overbite and suggests a Herbst appliance or Forsus, calling Herbst more effective.[31]
claims.experts: Wikipedia describes aligners as indicated mainly for mild to moderate crowding or spacing of about 1 to 6 mm without jaw discrepancies and as less effective than braces for some movements.[1] A 2023 systematic review compared aligners with fixed appliances in complicated and severe malocclusions.[19]

claims.claim: Aligners (or braces) will not fix a recessed jaw or maxilla, so surgery is needed.
claims.believers: A looksmax.org poster says an orthodontist told them aligners do the same as braces, would require wisdom tooth extraction first, and could let the lower jaw come forward; a replier calls this "holy cope" and recommends bimaxillary surgery.[32]
claims.experts: Wikipedia states aligners are indicated for cases without jaw-bone discrepancies.[1] The sources reviewed describe tooth movement outcomes and do not evaluate aligners as a treatment for skeletal jaw position.[5][7]
